newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Heavy fighting reported in north Afghan province.
newsitem.headline: Heavy fighting reported in north Afghan province.

text.p: The Taleban Islamic militia clashed with opposition forces in the northern Afghan province of Kunduz for the second day on Thursday, causing heavy civilian casualties, an aid worker said.

"Since yesterday, intense fighting continued around Kunduz (city) and the civilian casualty figure has gone up as the city itself has been the target of heavy shelling," the aid worker told Reuters from the northern city of Mazar-i-Sharif.

Kunduz city, the provincial capital 340 km (212 miles) north of Kabul, fell to the Taleban last month when a local opposition commander revolted against forces loyal to ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani.
Efforts for negotiations between the defecting commander and former government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood over the Taleban presence in Kunduz had failed, the aid worker said.
Masood wanted an evacuation of the Taleban's nearly 2,000 fighters in Kunduz but no serious fighting emerged until Wednesday, said the aid worker, who spoke on condition of anonymity.

The Taleban entered the neighbouring province of Takhar on Tuesday and said they had captured the provincial capital Taloqan, which has served as Rabbani's headquarters after the Taleban ousted him from Kabul last September.
But a Masood spokesman denied the claim.
The aid worker said Masood's forces had overall control of the province.
He said the Taleban forces were also involved in heavy fighting with Masood's forces in Khanabad district in southeastern Kunduz where their supply line was considered fragile.
Several civilians were wounded in air raids by anti-Taleban forces in the centre of Kunduz city on Wednesday, he said.
The Taleban have vowed to impose strict Islamic rule across Afghanistan, a goal which their ethnic minority opponents in the north see as concealing a drive for Pashtun hegemony.
The Taleban now control more than two thirds of the country.
